# Asurada

> Asurada is a free, open-source (MIT) macOS app for developers who write code with AI agents. It docks to the edge of the screen, helps you review only the changes that matter, and commits and pushes in one click.

Website: https://asurada-4yq.pages.dev/
Source code: https://github.com/LuckyYunPeng/asurada
Download: https://github.com/LuckyYunPeng/asurada/releases/latest

## Why it exists

AI agents can change dozens of files in one round. Reading every line is unrealistic, tests and boilerplate bury the important lines, and committing, pushing and resolving conflicts break your focus. Asurada's goal is to keep the human understanding the project: filter out the noise, review the key changes, and automate the chores after review.

## Features

- Diff window: changed files in a directory tree, word-level inline diff, unified or split layout, filter by file name, open a file in your editor.
- Hide test files while reviewing (they are still committed).
- Colorblind-friendly mode (blue/orange instead of green/red).
- One-click commit and push. The commit message is a one-line Conventional Commit (for example `feat: add dark mode`), written in English or Chinese to match the interface language.
- Commit messages are generated by the local `pi` coding agent in a separate short-lived session, so diffs and git output never enter your main AI chat.
- If the remote has new commits, Asurada rebases and retries; on conflicts it rolls back and tells you, leaving the repository untouched.
- All local git projects in one panel, projects with uncommitted changes listed first.
- Collapses to a small tab at the screen edge that lights up when there are changes; global shortcut Control+E (configurable) shows or hides the panel.
- Optional confirmation before commit, light/dark appearance, English/Chinese interface, launch at login, in-app updates.

## Requirements

- A Mac with Apple Silicon.
- `git` and the `pi` coding agent installed and available in your shell PATH.

## FAQ

- Is Asurada free? Yes. It is free and open source under the MIT License.
- Does it work on Windows, Linux or Intel Macs? No. It currently supports Apple Silicon Macs only.
- Does it send my code anywhere? Asurada runs locally. The commit message is generated by your own local `pi` agent, which uses whatever model provider you configured in pi.
- Will hiding test files leave them out of the commit? No. Hiding only affects the review list; one click stages and commits all changes.
- Which languages are supported? The interface and generated commit messages are available in English and Simplified Chinese, defaulting to the system language.
